result.title: Quantifying Annotation Agreement in Object Detection with Optimal Transport
result.summary: Reliable validation of machine learning models is a crucial step in designing robust and trustworthy systems. Yet validation relies on annotated test sets treated as ground truth, even though annotations can be noisy or ambiguous. In object detection, sources may disagree on object presence, box location, or class label. Standard agreement metrics usually binarize box overlap before computing a summary score, obscuring the degree and structure of disagreement between annotation sets. Here, we study an Optimal Transport (OT)-based metric for measuring agreement between object detection annotations. Instead of binarizing bounding box overlap, this metric assigns graded costs to matched and unmatched labeled boxes. Through theoretical analysis and experiments on real and synthetically perturbed annotations, we show that OT captures graded changes in agreement and distinguishes annotation pairs that thresholded metrics score identically. Our results suggest that OT provides a richer measure of annotation agreement in object detection, especially for domains with many small or ambiguous objects. Such agreement estimates can support more reliable validation when labels are noisy or conflicting.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究用最优传输（OT）度量目标检测标注之间的一致性，不再对框重叠做二值化，而是对匹配与未匹配的框给出分级代价；通过理论分析和真实及合成扰动标注实验，说明 OT 能捕捉一致性的渐变，并区分被阈值指标判为相同的标注对。
AI.relevance_reason: 其 OT 集合匹配与分级代价思路可能为 latent 状态与视觉实体、视觉证据之间的软对齐和筛选提供可核查的方法线索，但原文目标在数据集验证而非 VLM 推理。
